entries.title: Built-in llama provider login, environment resolution and catalog publication
entries.what: Expose loaded llama.cpp router models through the ordinary provider/model interfaces, with optional API-key login and cached catalog restoration. Configuring a compatible inference URL alone does not reproduce this provider's discovery and auth rules.
entries.interfaces: Provider/API llama.cpp/openai-completions; default router http://127.0.0.1:8080; environment LLAMA_BASE_URL,LLAMA_API_KEY; optional api_key credential with env.LLAMA_BASE_URL; getModels,refreshModels,stream,streamSimple; LlamaProviderController.setCatalog. Login is the generic /login llama.cpp flow, not a /llama login subcommand.

entries.title: Interactive llama model manager, search and cancellation recovery
entries.what: Provide an interactive model manager that can inspect the router, choose load/unload behavior, search and download GGUF models, and recover previously loaded models when a replacement is cancelled.
entries.interfaces: Command /llama (TUI only; args ignored); /login llama.cpp uses the generic auth flow. UI methods showModels/select/confirm/connectionError/searchModels/showStatus/progress/updateProgress. Action union model|download|close. Selection keys tui.select.up/down/confirm/cancel, search debounce500ms, minimum2 chars, visible10/12 rows, progress width40.

entries.title: Single-shot text prompts, final-message output and cleanup
entries.what: Run initial and additional prompts sequentially, print the final session message's text, and dispose the runtime once. Native text mode already works, but its retained-message state can print an earlier answer after the final prompt fails.
entries.interfaces: runPrintMode(runtimeHost,{mode:'text'|'json',messages?,initialMessage?,initialImages?})→Promise<number>. Text success returns 0, final assistant error/aborted or caught exception returns 1; signal exits are 129/143. Extension command context is rebound through the runtime host.

entries.title: Cancellation linking, waiter races and abortable timer lifetime
entries.what: Link an operation to a caller's cancellation signal and stop waiting promptly without abandoning the underlying promise's rejection. Timer and listener ownership are part of the contract, while Rust uses cancellation tokens and dropped futures instead of JavaScript promises.
entries.interfaces: linkAbortSignal(source?:AbortSignal,target:AbortController)→unlink; operationSignal(signal?:AbortSignal)→AbortSignal; raceWithAbort<T>(operation:Promise<T>,signal?:AbortSignal)→Promise<T>; sleep(ms:number,signal?:AbortSignal)→Promise<void>. Cancellation can carry any JS reason; absence of a reason has a named AbortError fallback only in abort.ts.

entries.title: Extension direct-process execution API and captured working directory
entries.what: Let trusted extension code run a command with an argument vector and collect separate stdout/stderr plus its exit result.

entries.title: User Bash execution helper and its distinct output contract
entries.what: User-entered shell commands produce live readable text, cancellation/exit metadata and a temporary full-output path without a model tool call. This helper has a different sanitation and buffering policy from model Bash.
entries.interfaces: executeBash(command:string,cwd:string,{onChunk?,signal?}) and executeBashWithOperations(command,cwd,operations,options). BashOperations is the same injectable execution interface used by TOOLS-001/002. Output has {output:string,exitCode?:number,cancelled:boolean,truncated:boolean,fullOutputPath?:string}. No timeout option is accepted by this helper. The user-facing !/!! dispatch and session persistence belong to session integration.

entries.title: Direct argv execution with capture, cancellation and timeout result
entries.what: Extension callers can execute an exact executable-plus-arguments array, capture stdout/stderr separately, and receive a result even on spawn failure or timeout.

entries.title: Image signatures, conversion, resizing and coordinate hints
entries.what: Image reads attach supported content within model size limits, convert BMP when necessary, and tell the model how displayed coordinates map back to the original image.
entries.interfaces: detectSupportedImageMimeType(bytes) -> image/jpeg|image/png|image/gif|image/webp|image/bmp|undefined; processImage(bytes,mime,{autoResizeImages?}) -> {ok:true,data,mimeType,hints}|{ok:false,message}; resizeImage(bytes,mime,{maxWidth?,maxHeight?,maxBytes?,jpegQuality?}) -> {data,mimeType,width,height,originalWidth,originalHeight,wasResized}|null; formatDimensionNote(result). ReadImageProcessor returns base64 image content plus optional explanatory text. External dependency: @silvia-odwyer/photon-node WASM in TS; no network service is contacted by the image pipeline.

entries.title: Package source grammar, canonical identity and scoped local-path resolution
entries.what: Users can identify extension/resource packages with npm specifications, Git repositories with optional refs, or local files/directories. The parser determines cache identity and pin behavior before any install or settings mutation.
entries.interfaces: Source strings include npm:name[@version], npm:@scope/name[@version], git:host/owner/repo[@ref], explicit git:git@host:owner/repo[@ref], protocol Git URLs, relative/absolute/home/file-URL local paths. GitSource carries repo, host, path, optional ref and pinned. Stable identity must be reused by add/remove/update and scoped dedup; it must not silently turn a bare local name into an npm or Git source.

entries.title: Distribution identity, agent roots and bundled resource path resolution
entries.what: Every settings, resource and session consumer resolves a consistent distribution identity and directory tree, whether ICE runs from TypeScript, a package installation or a Bun binary. Environment overrides and resource assets have explicit path rules.
entries.source: ice:packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts:21-25,369-605 getPackageDir, asset/path helpers and identity constants; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/paths.ts:1-119 normalizePath/resolvePath/canonicalPath; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/legacy-compat/paths.ts:1-7; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/legacy-compat/env.ts:1-32; ice:packages/coding-agent/docs/environment-variables.md:1-89.
entries.interfaces: Exports include isBunBinary,isBunRuntime,getPackageDir,getThemesDir,getExportTemplateDir,getPackageJsonPath,getReadmePath,getDocsPath,getExamplesPath,getChangelogPath,getInteractiveAssetsDir,getCogneeSkillsDir,getObserveDashboardPath,getBundledInteractiveAssetPath,expandTildePath,getShareViewerUrl,getAgentDir,getProjectConfigDir,getCustomThemesDir,getModelsPath,getAuthPath,getSettingsPath,getToolsDir,getBinDir,getPromptsDir,getSessionsDir,getDebugLogPath. Identity fields are PACKAGE_NAME,APP_NAME,APP_TITLE,CONFIG_DIR_NAME,VERSION,ENV_AGENT_DIR,ENV_SESSION_DIR. No migration or directory creation is implied by a path getter.

entries.title: Tool path normalization and ordered read-path fallback
entries.what: Tool calls accept user-style paths and locate common macOS screenshot spellings while keeping write/edit destinations literal after normalization.
entries.interfaces: expandPath,resolveToCwd,resolveReadPath,resolveReadPathAsync,pathExists; harness normalizeToolPath,resolveToolPath,resolveReadToolPath. Shared normalizePath options {trim?,expandTilde?,homeDir?,stripAtPrefix?,normalizeUnicodeSpaces?}; tool callers enable stripAtPrefix and normalizeUnicodeSpaces. Inputs remain strings, and errors from file URLs or harness filesystem operations can reject the tool.
